evals.prompt: Please peer-review my manuscript. Run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/minimal.tex
evals.expected_output: The skill checks for the review/addition-suggestion environments (they are absent), shows a preamble patch and asks for approval, extracts manuscript paragraphs, generates 3-8 review comments with suggestions, shows a diff preview of the injections, and (after approval) writes the environments and review blocks into the .tex file.
expectations: The output .tex file contains \newenvironment{review}
The output .tex file contains \newenvironment{addition-suggestion}
The output .tex file contains at least one \begin{review} block
The output .tex file contains at least one \begin{addition-suggestion} block
The skill asked for approval before writing (showed a diff or patch preview)
No full review text was printed as plain terminal output (it was injected into the file)

evals.prompt: Peer-review my paper without suggestions. Run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/minimal.tex --no-suggest
evals.expected_output: The skill injects review blocks but NOT addition-suggestion blocks. The preamble still gets both environment definitions (they may be needed later). Review comments appear after relevant paragraphs.
expectations: The output .tex file contains at least one \begin{review} block
The output .tex file does NOT contain any \begin{addition-suggestion} block
The skill asked for approval before writing

evals.prompt: Review this manuscript which already has the environments defined. Run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/full-preamble.tex
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that both environments are already defined and does NOT add duplicate definitions. It proceeds directly to extraction and review without patching the preamble. The final .tex has exactly one definition of each environment.
expectations: The output .tex file contains exactly one occurrence of \newenvironment{review}
The output .tex file contains exactly one occurrence of \newenvironment{addition-suggestion}
The output .tex file contains at least one \begin{review} block

evals.prompt: Do a dry-run peer review of my manuscript. Run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/minimal.tex --dry-run
evals.expected_output: The skill prints a unified diff showing what would be inserted, but does NOT modify the .tex file. The original file content is unchanged after the run.
expectations: A unified diff is shown in the output (lines starting with + appear)
The original minimal.tex file is unchanged (its content does not contain \begin{review})

evals.prompt: Expert peer-review of my manuscript with project context. Run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/expert-draft.tex --expert --project evals/fixtures/project-expert
evals.expected_output: The skill reads manuscript-context.md, loads methods/results context, and produces review comments that reference specific parameters (PBE-D3, 830 eV cutoff, RASPA2 GCMC, TraPPE-UA, counterpoise correction) rather than generic 'specify your DFT method'. Comments address known weaknesses (Al substitution, TraPPE-UA transferability, rigid framework) from manuscript-context.md. Review injected into .tex file.
expectations: The output .tex file contains at least one \begin{review} block
At least one review comment references a specific parameter from manuscript-context.md (e.g. PBE-D3, 830 eV, TraPPE-UA, RASPA2, counterpoise, or BSSE)
At least one review comment addresses a known weakness from manuscript-context.md (Al substitution, TraPPE-UA transferability, or rigid framework)
No warning about missing manuscript-context.md appears

evals.prompt: Expert peer-review without manuscript context. Run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/expert-draft.tex --expert --project evals/fixtures/project-no-context
evals.expected_output: The skill finds no manuscript-context.md in the project dir, prints the fallback warning message telling the user to run /open-manuscript, falls back to memory files, and still produces a review (generic but functional).
expectations: A warning message appears mentioning 'manuscript-context.md not found' or 'Falling back'
The output .tex file contains at least one \begin{review} block
The warning recommends running /open-manuscript

evals.prompt: Seeded-recall A/B protocol: run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/seeded-a.tex --passes 1 (arm A) and record the review JSON to evals/runs/, repeat on evals/fixtures/seeded-b.tex for both arms, then run python3 evals/run_seeded_recall.py --arm-a <arm-a.json> --arm-b <arm-b.json>.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the review under each arm (arm A = single pass, arm B = three passes with synopsis and synthesis), the agent records each arm's comment set as JSON without any LLM call inside the harness, and run_seeded_recall.py prints a recall@N table per defect type (missing_scf_criterion, section_inversion, abstract_overclaim, new_claim_in_conclusions, absent_data_availability) for both arms, the A/B verdict line, and a C5 precision pass over every produced comment set.
expectations: The recall table lists all 5 seeded defect types with A and B hit counts
The verdict line reports B >= A overall and whether B loses any type A catches
Every produced comment set passes check_reviews.py precision (RESULT: OK)
The harness itself makes no LLM calls (it only scores recorded arm JSONs)

evals.expected_output: The skill loads the Journal-Specific Standards subsection of reporting_standards.md plus references/journals/nature.md when present, calibrates severity so format and fit violations become major, and shows the dry-run diff without writing.
expectations: The journal calibration is applied because the --journal flag takes precedence over manuscript-context.md and the default
Format/fit violations are commented at severity major
The original .tex file is unchanged (dry-run only)

evals.expected_output: The skill skips journal format constraints (Lens 7 format items), downgrades Lens 1d structural balance to a signal, and adds the AI-unreliable caveat to any novelty comment, still producing a dry-run diff without writing.
expectations: No format-compliance comments are produced in --preprint mode
Novelty comments carry the explicit AI-unreliable caveat
The original .tex file is unchanged (dry-run only)

evals.expected_output: The skill skips Step 4 expert context entirely (no manuscript-context.md lookup, no project memory, no fallback warning), simulating a fresh external reviewer, while references condensation still runs, and shows the dry-run diff.
expectations: No manuscript-context.md warning or /open-manuscript recommendation appears
References condensation is still applied (it is public knowledge a real reviewer has)
The original .tex file is unchanged (dry-run only)

evals.prompt: Claim extraction pre-filter: run python3 scripts/extract_manuscript.py --file evals/fixtures/seeded-a.tex --claims
evals.expected_output: The script prints a JSON object containing the unchanged paragraphs array (C1) plus a claims array of heuristic candidates covering regex patterns for we show/demonstrate/report/find, number+unit strings, and significance terms, pre-filtering the input for Step 4b and the Lens 3 claim-evidence check.
expectations: The output is an object with a paragraphs list and a non-empty claims list
Claims include the we-show style sentence from the introduction
Claims include a number+unit candidate (e.g. the 520 eV cutoff or 1.9 W m-1 K-1)
Without --claims the output stays the plain C1 array (backward compatible)

evals.prompt: R&R resolution check: run python3 scripts/check_review_envs.py --check-resolved --file <previously reviewed .tex> --reviews <synthesis C4.json>
evals.expected_output: The script scans the injected review environments against the current paragraph text and prints one entry per comment with id, status (resolved|unresolved|uncertain) and matched_quote, so the agent can see which round-one comments the revision addressed.
expectations: Every comment id from the reviews JSON appears in the output
Each status is one of resolved, unresolved, uncertain
matched_quote is a string (empty or the span found in the current text)
Both claudeorange and reviewcolor manuscripts are accepted

evals.prompt: Pass-count knob: run /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/minimal.tex --passes 1 --dry-run and then /peer-review --file evals/fixtures/minimal.tex --passes 3 --dry-run
evals.expected_output: With --passes 1 the skill runs one review call covering all lenses with no Step 4b synopsis (the v1-equivalent A arm). With --passes 3 (the default) it runs Step 4b synopsis, three sequential reviewer passes, and Step 5e synthesis before injection.
expectations: --passes 1 produces a single review pass with no synopsis step
--passes 3 produces synopsis plus three reviewer passes plus synthesis
Both runs stay sequential in-pane (no subagent spawning)
Both runs show the diff and write nothing (dry-run)
